newsitem.title: JAPAN: TIFFE euroyen futures end higher in line with JGBs.
newsitem.headline: TIFFE euroyen futures end higher in line with JGBs.

text.p: April 22 settlement prev settlement
TIFFE Euroyen 3M (Z) 99.08 99.05
Key December three-month euroyen deposit rate futures ended Tuesday's TIFFE day session higher in line with small gains in Japanese government bond (JGB) futures.
The December contract settled at 99.08, after trading between 99.06 and 99.08. Turnover was a meagre 16,363 lots.
"Euroyen futures firmed in line with JGBs, but were still stuck in a narrow range," said a brokerage house trader.
Key June JGB futures ended up 0.07 at 126.98.
Traders said euroyen futures' upside was heavy because cash rates were hovering at high levels.
The cash three-month euroyen deposit rate was quoted at 0.58/0.57 percent, virtually flat from 0.58/0.56 percent on late Monday.
"While cash rates remain stuck at the current high level, euroyen futures are likely to have a limited upside," said the trader.
Traders said euroyen futures also have limited downside potential due to a lack of fresh sell factors.
In the morning session, some selling emerged after the Bank of Japan's (BOJ) regular money market operation, but only briefly, traders said.
The BOJ maintained an accommodative stance on Tuesday by injecting a net 200 billion yen against a projected surplus of about 10 billion yen.
However, the key unsecured overnight call rate edged up as market participants had expected the central bank to inject about 300 billion yen, traders said.
Traders predict Tuesday's weighted average of the call rate to be around 0.53 percent, up from Monday's 0.51 percent.
Traders said the motives behind recent heavy trades in June euroyen futures put options with a strike price of 99.25 on SIMEX remained a mystery.
There is talk that hedge funds may have been behind buying of these put options, they said.
About 11,000 lots of these options, due to expire on June 16, were traded on Monday on SIMEX, but no trades have been seen on Tuesday.
In the interest rate swap (IRS) market, some city banks showed interest in receiving two- to three-year fixed interest rates, traders said.
However, IRS rates were little changed across the yield curve by late Tuesday.

About 50 billion yen worth of three-month certificates of deposit (CDs) were issued at 0.56 percent after about 20 billion yen worth were issued earlier at 0.55 percent. Three-month CDs were being offered at 0.55 percent on Monday.
About 40 billion yen worth of one-month CDs were issued at 0.54 percent, up from 0.53 percent on Monday.
Two-month CDs were offered at 0.54 percent, flat from the previous session.
-- Kanta Watanabe, Tokyo Treasury Desk +81-3-3432-9780
